official.deadline_note: The 2026/2027 call ran 15 November to 15 December 2025 on the PAU submission portal; the portal now states applications closed on 15/12/2025. No opening or closing dates for the following cycle have been published yet.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year cycle (call launched 15 November 2025, closed 15 December 2025)
official.status_note: The PAU application platform banner reads 'Applications closed on 15/12/2025', and the African Union Commission announcement states the call closed on 15 December 2025 and that applications received after the deadline will NOT be considered.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Pan African University states: 'The PAU offers full scholarships (covering tuition and living expenses) for all successful applicants in all its institutes.' The African Union Commission announcement states: 'The African Union Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates.'
benefits: Full scholarship awarded by the African Union Commission to successful candidates
Joint degree awards from the Pan African University and its host universities
Students' medical insurance covered from disbursed stipends by each PAU institute
Study at one of four PAU institutes hosted by JKUAT (Kenya), University of Ibadan (Nigeria), University of Yaounde II / University of Buea (Cameroon) and University of Tlemcen (Algeria)
eligibility: Young, qualified, talented and enterprising applicants from African countries and the Diaspora are invited to apply
Master's applicants: not older than 25 years (male) and 28 years (female)
Master's applicants: holder of an undergraduate degree from a recognised university with at least a second-class upper division or its equivalent, in a relevant field
PhD applicants: maximum 28 years old (male) and 30 years old (female)
PhD applicants: a master's degree in a relevant field from PAU or any internationally recognised university
As the PAU programmes are residential and full-time, civil servants and employees of private or public companies are not admitted, as well as students already receiving a scholarship
Scholarship awardees should be committed to working in Africa after graduation

Master's candidates for Conference Interpreting and Translation must have excellent knowledge of at least two African Union official languages (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese, Kiswahili, Spanish)
requirements: Certified true copies of relevant certificates and transcripts (from university and high school)
Passport or national identity card (personal details page)
Detailed CV mentioning professional experience, trainings, workshops, conferences, publications and language skills
Cover letter stating the reasons for applying to the PAU programmes
Master's: one recommendation letter from a former university lecturer (Full Professor or Senior Lecturer)
PhD: two recommendation letters from two different Professors (Full Professors or Senior Lecturers)
PhD: concept note of maximum four pages
Names of three reference university lecturers with email address and WhatsApp number (mandatory), distinct from the recommending lecturers
All diploma and document copies must be translated and submitted in either English or French
All documents must be scanned in PDF format, each under 2 MB; the identity picture must be in JPG/JPEG format, also under 2 MB
Candidates may be required to undergo a written or oral examination after pre-selection
documents: Certified copies of degrees and transcripts (university and high school), accompanied by transcripts
Passport or national identity card, personal details page
2cm x 2cm coloured passport photograph (JPG/JPEG, under 2 MB)
Cover letter addressed to the Rector of the Pan African University
Academic recommendation letter(s) addressed to the Rector of the Pan African University
Research concept note, maximum four pages (PhD applicants only)
Names and contact details of three academic referees
Scanned PDF copies of all documents, each under 2 MB
selection_criteria: Academic competence must be evidenced in academic transcripts at the bachelor's level
Candidates may be required to undergo a written or oral examination after pre-selection
Results are communicated about two months after the closing date, by letter of approval to successful applicants only
coverage: The PAU offers full scholarships covering tuition and living expenses for all successful applicants in all its institutes
Each PAU institute ensures students' medical insurance is covered from disbursed stipends
application_method: Complete the application online only at https://www.au-pau.org/submission/ (no postal applications are accepted)
Register with a valid username and email, confirm registration via the confirmation link, set a password, then log in
Open the Application page, provide all data, click Save after each step and click FINISH when complete
The scholarship agreement requires an undertaking to serve an African Union Member State for a period at least equal to the duration of the scholarship after successful completion of studies
official.application_route: Online only through the PAU submission portal at https://www.au-pau.org/submission/ - register, confirm by email, log in, complete the Application page and press FINISH before the deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from African countries and the African Diaspora; the FAQ states any African student living in Africa or in the Diaspora who meets the eligibility criteria is eligible
official.international_eligibility: Open to African applicants, including those in the Diaspora; not open to non-African applicants
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Programme choice is limited to one programme at one of the four PAU institutes (PAUSTI Kenya, PAULESI Nigeria, PAUGHSS Cameroon, PAUWES Algeria); Master's in Conference Interpreting and Translation additionally requires excellent knowledge of at least two African Union official languages (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese, Kiswahili, Spanish)
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a 3 to 4-page research concept note (tentative title, research questions, objectives, significance of the research) of maximum four pages
official.description: The Pan African University is a Premier continental university network initiative of the Heads of State and Government of the African Union, whose mission is to provide quality postgraduate education geared towards the achievement of a prosperous, integrated and peaceful Africa. Young, qualified, talented and enterprising applicants from African countries and the Diaspora are invited to join master's or PhD programmes at any of its four institutes. From 2014 to date PAU has issued 2549 certificates - 856 to females and 1693 to males - involving students from 50 Member States.
official.program_type: Continental intergovernmental postgraduate scholarship (African Union Commission / Pan African University)

verification.notes: Checked the African Union Commission announcement for the 2026/2027 call, the PAU submission portal home page and its full FAQ, and the official Pan African University scholarships page. The official sources state full scholarships covering tuition and living expenses but publish no stipend figure, currency or per-period amount, no travel allowance, and no English language test requirement; the 2026/2027 round closed on 15 December 2025.

applicant_utility.summary: The 2026/2027 round closed on 15 December 2025 and the portal banner still reads 'Applications closed', so treat this as a once-a-year window that historically opens on 15 November and target the next call rather than the closed one. The award covers tuition and living expenses but the awarding body publishes no stipend amount, so budget separately for flights, visas, settling in and personal spending. You may apply to exactly one programme at one institute, and the application locks the moment you press FINISH, so upload everything first. Awardees must serve an African Union Member State for a period at least as long as the scholarship after graduating, which is a serious commitment to weigh before applying.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent African graduates or master's holders inside the 25/28 (master's) or 28/30 (PhD) age caps who want a residential continental postgraduate degree and can commit to post-study service in Africa.
application_readiness_checklist: Scan every certificate and transcript as a separate PDF under 2 MB, with the passport photo as JPG/JPEG under 2 MB
Have each diploma certified by the university that issued it, and pair every diploma with its transcript
Line up three referee lecturers with email addresses and WhatsApp numbers who are different people from your recommending lecturer(s)
Brief your recommending professor so the letter lands in English or French and is addressed to the Rector of the Pan African University
Draft the cover letter explaining your motivation for PAU, and for PhD a concept note of no more than four pages
Confirm your degree has actually been conferred - a testimonial or pending certificate is not accepted
Use the latest Chrome or Firefox from a wired connection, with ad blocker, proxy and VPN switched off
common_rejection_risks: Registering or applying for more than one programme - any attempt at multiple registrations is nullified
Pressing FINISH with documents still missing or unreadable; the form cannot be edited afterwards and reopening needs an email to support
Applying while your bachelor's or master's diploma has not yet been issued, or sending uncertified copies
Submitting documents that are not translated into English or French, or files exceeding the 2 MB limit
Being a civil servant, an employee of a private or public company, or already holding another scholarship - all three are excluded
Ignoring the age caps, which are strict at 25/28 for master's and 28/30 for PhD
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The call does not publish a stipend figure or any travel, installation or relocation allowance, so applicants must fund their own flights to the host country, visa and immigration costs, initial settling-in expenses, clothing and personal items, and any costs beyond what the living-expense component provides. Medical insurance is covered from the disbursed stipend rather than added on top.
document_audit: Transcripts must be attached to diplomas - a diploma alone is treated as incomplete
Only certified copies are needed; never send originals through the portal
Recommendation letters must come from a Full Professor or Senior Lecturer: one for master's, two different professors for PhD
The three referee lecturers named in the form must not be the same people who wrote your recommendation letters
The CV must spell out language skills in French, English, Arabic and Portuguese plus trainings, conferences and publications
The passport photograph is the only file expected in JPG/JPEG; everything else should be PDF
alerts: The portal is currently closed and no dates for the next round have been announced - watch the PAU platform and the African Union announcements page rather than relying on third-party deadline sites
Awardees must serve an African Union Member State for at least as long as the scholarship lasted, and may not take income-generating work that interferes with their studies without Rectorate approval
Results arrive only about two months after the closing date, and silence means unsuccessful - do not build other plans around a faster reply
Once FINISH is clicked the application cannot be edited, and reopening it by email must be done WITHOUT attaching any documents
A pre-selection examination (written or oral) may follow, so keep academic transcripts strong rather than relying only on paperwork
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the PAU portal with a valid email, confirm via the emailed link, set a password, log in, fill the Application page saving after each upload, then tick the agreement and click FINISH before the deadline; an application number and success message confirm receipt.
